name: CORE (Common Open Research Emulator)
what_it_is: CORE is a network emulation tool that uses Linux network namespaces to emulate networked systems on one or more machines. It supports connecting emulated networks to live networks and provides both a graphical topology editor and Python scripting modules for programmatic simulation.
measurement: No built-in measurement or monitoring tooling documented in README
Hybrid live-network connectivity enables external measurement tools to be attached
configuration: Installation via pre-built deb/rpm packages or source-based install scripts
Virtual environment installed at /opt/core/venv for package installs
Graphical topology editor for visual node/link configuration
Python scripting API for programmatic topology definition
fault_injection: No fault injection mechanism documented in README or repository surface
modes: Scripted (Python API for automated topology creation)
Hybrid (emulated nodes connected to live physical networks)
constraints: Requires Linux (uses Linux network namespaces — not portable to macOS/Windows natively)
No docker-compose.yml found on master branch — containerised deployment not officially documented in repo root
EMANE integration requires separate EMANE installation
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in repository root (404 on master branch)
No built-in fault injection support documented
No native measurement or telemetry collection pipeline
No Windows or macOS support (Linux namespaces dependency)
No documented scalability limits or node count constraints in README
